analysis.title: Global Economics Wrap-Up: November 20, 2026
key_insights: DM inflation progress was slower than expected in 2026 because of Middle East conflict price pressures, continued tariff passthrough and AI demand-related price increases. GS still expects inflation to slow in 2027, with some near-term upside risk from energy and upstream costs.
October DM inflation data was mixed. US CPI surprised to the upside, Euro area inflation was revised up to 4.03%, and UK headline CPI rose to 3.6%. Canada and Japan surprised to the downside.
GS expects 0.29% m/m for October US core PCE, released next Wednesday, following this week's import price release.
GS 2027 US Outlook: GDP growth of 2.4%, modestly above consensus, driven by solid consumption and strong business investment, offset by housing and trade drags.
GS expects a low-hire, low-fire labor market in 2027, with AI displacement pushing unemployment higher in later years.
GS expects core PCE inflation to fall to 2.4% by late 2027 as tariff, Iran war energy shock and AI price effects fade.

GS forecasts two more 25bp Fed hikes in December and March to 4.25-4.5%, then gradual cuts to 3.25-3.5% starting November 2027. It does not expect major institutional changes from the Fed task forces, though a shift toward bills on the balance sheet is possible.
Fed speakers this week were split. Williams pushed back against a 50bp December hike, while Hammack, Musalem and Goolsbee sounded more hawkish.

UK 2027 outlook: the energy shock hits consumer spending over the winter and inflation rises further as utility bills increase. GS is still constructive on 2027 because of structural growth improvement, stronger productivity and likely further fiscal consolidation.
Country outlooks for 2027: France faces presidential and likely parliamentary elections, Italy is losing momentum, and German growth was robust in 2026 but has limited upside.
UK data was mixed. Unemployment fell to 4.6% in September, but flash October payrolls showed a 34k fall in employment. Retail sales rebounded 0.7% m/m in October.
China October activity data weakened and missed expectations. Industrial production slowed to 4.8% y/y, fixed asset investment fell 16.3% y/y and retail sales growth slowed to 0.4% y/y.
China's Q3 current account surplus widened to 5.0% of GDP from 3.6% in Q2, and October net FX inflows of US$70bn were the largest monthly inflow since January 2026.

Bank Indonesia surprised with a 25bp hike to 6% to support the rupiah, and GS expects one more 25bp hike in Q1 2027. South Africa held at 7.25% and GS expects a 25bp hike in January. Hungary held at 5.5%.
GS GDP tracker has 2027 US growth at 2.4% and euro area at 1.3%, with China at 4.5% and India at 6.6% in the forecast columns shown.

risk_factors: Longer-lasting oil or AI price pressures or new shocks could keep inflation higher.
A larger tightening in financial conditions or earlier and more rapid AI job displacement could weigh on growth.
Near-term upside inflation risk from higher energy prices and upstream cost increases.
UK consumer spending faces an energy shock over the winter and a difficult Spending Review.
Overheating risk from the AI buildout and persistent tariff effects, as cited by Goolsbee.
geopolitical: Middle East conflict price pressures and the Iran war energy shock are cited as drivers of slower DM disinflation.
France presidential and likely parliamentary elections in 2027 carry wide-ranging implications for the economy, fiscal policy and markets.
Tariff passthrough continues to add to US inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Williams pushed back against a 50bp December hike and called firmer October CPI a continuation, not a broadening, of tariff and energy effects. Jefferson's focus on trends hints at a gradual pace.
tension_points.bear_case: Hammack wants restriction put back in the economy, and Musalem said several increases are needed before spring 2027 to reach 2% inflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further upside inflation surprise, such as October core PCE above GS's 0.29% m/m estimate, would raise the odds of a faster pace than 25bp increments.
